text:
alice: FYI ap-southeast1 nvme pool showing persistent tiny-write storm since ~03:20 UTC, observed multiple GPU attach fails and scheduler backpressure. Anyone oncall?
ops-bot: INCIDENT ap-southeast1 small_write_iops_percentile_99 78% > warning (hosts: nvmepool-12..16) :warning:
ben: i'm on it, grabbing iostat and kernel blk stats. initial glance: write Q depth spikes, fsync-heavy patterns. attaching short snippet.
dave: small sample from host nvmepool-13: ```iostat -x 1 3
Device: rrqm/s wrqm/s r/s w/s  rMB/s  wMB/s  avgrq-sz  avgqu-sz  await  r_await  w_await  svctm  %util
nvme0n1 0.00 0.00 12.00 18000.00 0.01 120.5 6.7 45.2 12.4 0.6 12.8 0.10 95.3
```
carol: pattern smells like janitor overlap with short-lived training checkpoints. Janitors doing lots of small deletes + metadata fsync. Short term: 1) scale janitor down in region 2) mark a couple racks DRAIN for batch 3) bump ephemeral eviction batch size to coalesce writes
maya: quick cost estimate: draining and requeuing batches will push jobs to other regions -> extra egress + spot premium ~ +$2k/hr if sustained. Throttling janitor is near-zero cost.
leo: I can flip the janitor concurrency flag and pause scheduler quickly. Recommend workers 8->2 for 30m and pause batch-scheduler for 15m.
ben: commands: ```PATCH /flags/janitor {"region":"ap-southeast1","concurrency":2}``` and ```POST /scheduler/pause {"region":"ap-southeast1","reason":"io_surge","mins":15}```. I'll run and monitor.
dave: kicked a SMART scan to check for early wear indicators: `ansible apse1 -m shell -a "nvme smart-log /dev/nvme* | tee /var/log/nvme-smart/scan-$(date +%s).log"`. No immediate SMART errors but wear_level% slightly high on nvmepool-15.
carol: update runbook: add threshold rule. If 99p small-write iops > 15k AND attach_failures > 3 in 10m -> throttle janitor, pause scheduler, open ticket to infra-sre. I'll PR the runbook after stabilization.
alice: do it. ben/leo make the changes now. dave follow up with wear scans and post results. maya file a cost impact note in finance if we escalate to cross-region failover. create follow-up TICKET-3421 to investigate mitigation: rewrite janitor to coalesce, enable write coalescing at VFS layer, per-pool min-evict-delay.
ben: applied flags and paused scheduler. graphs show 99p write_iops dropping to ~5k in 3m and attach failures returning to baseline.
leo: staying oncall for 60m, will escalate to oncall rotation if errors recur. leaving a short postmortem stub TICKET-3422 with timeline. :thumbsup:
alice: thanks. after 60m reconvene and decide on medium-term change (per-pool eviction limits + janitor rewrite).
